newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom to get free investment hand.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom to get free investment hand.

text.p: France Telecom will have a free hand in investment decisions, currently subject to state approval, when it is partially privatised next year, Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon said.
He said the telecommunications operator needed the same management freedom as its competitors and would no longer require permission from the state Economic and Social Development Fund to invest.
Fillon told an industry forum on Tuesday that France Telecom's planned investment would decline to 26 billion francs next year from 31.6 billion in 1995.
France Telecom chairman Michel Bon said the decline was due both to past modernisation efforts and the falling cost of equipment.

"I note that France Telecom's main rivals, already subject to competition, such as British Telecom are investing massively in high technology...and are preparing for tomorrow's competition," Fillon said.

"France Telecom must not rest on its laurels but on the contrary...invest in the technologies of the future. And if it doesn't do so, you can bet the markets which watch its strategy will remind it," he said.
The minister acknowledged that the decline in France Telecom's investment could cause problems for suppliers but said they should be only temporary.
"In fact, telecommunications industrialists have every reason to hope that the opening to competition will breathe new life into their sector," he said.
